subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should Memory Wiki intentionally impose a 1 MiB maximum on previously accepted `wiki apply synthesis --body-file` input, and if so what upgrade or alternative path should users with larger synthesis bodies receive?
rationale: The diff resolves an implementation concern by adding a new public rejection policy; source-level tests cannot determine whether that compatibility tradeoff is the intended product contract.

options.title: Preserve existing input compatibility
options.body: Replace the arbitrary public cap with a bounded implementation that follows an established gateway or synthesis-body contract without rejecting currently valid larger files.

options.title: Adopt the 1 MiB contract
options.body: Keep the rejection only after an owner confirms the limit, documents the supported larger-body workflow or migration, and accepts the compatibility impact.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Leave the current behavior unchanged until the desired Memory Wiki input policy is decided.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing input compatibility
recommendation.body: Replace the arbitrary public cap with a bounded implementation that follows an established gateway or synthesis-body contract without rejecting currently valid larger files.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied timeline includes a direct escalation to steipete, making them the strongest available routing candidate for the public-policy decision.
